text:
Minnesota won its third straight game, but the Wild got there in an odd way: Jesper Wallstedt carried them through a third period in which Utah was the far better team. Wallstedt, drafted 20th overall in 2021 out of Luleå HF, stopped 26 of 27 shots. By our numbers he saved about two goals more than the quality of those shots should have allowed.

The score and the play did not match. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, came out at 2.96 for Utah and 2.88 for Minnesota, and our simulation had UTA deserving the win 52 percent of the time. Minnesota controlled the first two periods, 2.20 to 1.01 in expected goals, and scored twice on the power play, Joel Eriksson Ek on a snap shot late in the second and Kirill Kaprizov early in the third. Kaprizov's goal came on a 4 percent chance. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0 at 11:44 of the third, an even-strength goal on an 18 percent look.

Then Utah took over, out-chancing Minnesota 1.95 to 0.68 in the period. Logan Cooley had a 24 percent chance stopped by Wallstedt before scoring on a 45 percent look with 81 seconds left, far too late to matter. Karel Vejmelka was roughly even with the quality of shots he faced, so the gap came from Minnesota's special teams (2 for 7, to Utah's 0 for 4) and from Wallstedt. The Wild have won three in a row.
